Ingredients (I used half the portions)

250g baked pumpkin (instead of butternut squash)
125ml egg whites (4 egg whites)
17.5g cocoa powder
12.5g oat flour
25g chocolate chips (70%)
30–40g sweetener (stevia or monk fruit)
½ tsp vanilla
¼ tsp baking powder
Pinch of salt

Directions:

Roast the pumpkin cut-side down at 400°F / 200°C for about 35 minutes, or until soft. Let it cool, then remove the skin.

Add the baked pumpkin, egg whites, cocoa powder, oat flour, sweetener, vanilla, baking powder, and salt to a blender. Blend until smooth.

Pour into a baking dish, sprinkle the chocolate chips on top, and bake until set. Let it cool, then place it in the fridge. It tastes best cold.

Note: I had to keep it longer in the oven cause it was more liquid.

Estimated macros for the whole half-batch:
345 calories
23g protein
51g carbs
11g fat

If cut into 4 pieces:
86 calories
6g protein
13g carbs
3g fat

title: High-Protein Pumpkin Chocolate Brownie
one_liner: A low-calorie, high-protein pumpkin brownie made in a blender with egg whites and cocoa powder.
key_points: Only 86 calories and 6g protein per slice when cut into 4 pieces
Uses roasted pumpkin or butternut squash as the base instead of flour
Blends all ingredients together — no mixing bowls needed
Tastes best cold, straight from the fridge or on top of yogurt

instructions: Roast pumpkin cut-side down at 400°F / 200°C for ~35 minutes until soft. Let cool and remove skin.
Add pumpkin, egg whites, cocoa powder, oat flour, sweetener, vanilla, baking powder, and salt to a blender. Blend until smooth.
Pour batter into a baking dish, sprinkle chocolate chips on top, and bake until set (center should be slightly jiggly).
Let cool, then refrigerate. Serve cold, optionally on top of yogurt.
